evals.prompt: Review only the staged readability refactor in documents/canDownload.ts:12-22 and its changed tests with correctness lens. Before: `return document != null && !document.deleted && account.active && account.canRead(document.id) && audit.recordDownloadAttempt(document.id);`. After: `const readable = account.canRead(document.id); const audited = audit.recordDownloadAttempt(document.id); return [document != null, !document.deleted, account.active, readable, audited].every(Boolean);`. Inspected callers legally pass null when a document is absent and inactive accounts when access is denied. canRead performs a remote permission check and may throw; recordDownloadAttempt increments a persisted counter and returns true. The contract requires no remote check or audit when the document is absent, deleted, or the account inactive, and no audit if canRead rejects or throws. Existing tests verified these skipped effects; the refactor's tests cover only the all-true result. The implementer says named predicates and every(Boolean) are clearer. Give a concrete correctness report and behavior-preserving alternative without editing or adding unrelated maintainability lenses.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-backed correctness finding for eager decomposition that breaks null guards and effect timing, recommending restoration of lazy ordered checks rather than approving a readable but behavior-changing refactor.
expectations: The finding cites canDownload.ts:12-22 and demonstrates null document dereference before its guard, unwanted permission calls on deleted/inactive paths, and a persisted audit even when canRead returns false.
The report distinguishes the original permission-exception path, where audit is skipped, from the eager false-result path; it does not falsely claim audit runs after canRead throws.

The recommendation restores the original short-circuit chain or ordered early guards with lazy predicates at the original decision points, preserving evaluation order/count, side effects, exception timing and null safety without eager arrays, opaque helpers or a new framework/class.

Severity follows concrete null and persisted-effect impact, the uncovered rejection paths are identified without fabricating a test run, and the report remains bounded to correctness, read-only and advisory without an approval verdict.
